{{Short description|Homotopy operation}}
In mathematics, the '''Whitehead product''' is a [[Graded Lie algebra|graded]] [[quasi-Lie algebra]] structure on the [[homotopy group]]s of a space.  It was defined by [[J. H. C. Whitehead]] in {{harv|Whitehead|1941}}.

The relevant [[Mathematics Subject Classification|MSC]] code is: 55Q15, Whitehead products and generalizations.

== Definition ==
Given elements <math>f \in \pi_k(X), g \in \pi_l(X)</math>, the '''Whitehead bracket''' 

:<math>[f,g] \in \pi_{k+l-1}(X)</math>

is defined as follows:

The product <math>S^k \times S^l</math> can be obtained by attaching a <math>(k+l)</math>-cell to the [[wedge sum]]

:<math>S^k \vee S^l</math>;

the [[attaching map]] is a map 

:<math>S^{k+l-1} \stackrel{\phi}{\ \longrightarrow\ } S^k \vee S^l. </math>

Represent <math>f</math> and <math>g</math> by maps

:<math>f\colon S^k \to X </math>

and
:<math>g\colon S^l \to X, </math>

then compose their wedge with the attaching map, as

:<math>S^{k+l-1} \stackrel{\phi}{\ \longrightarrow\ } S^k \vee S^l \stackrel{f \vee g}{\ \longrightarrow\ } X .</math>

The [[homotopy class]] of the resulting map does not depend on the choices of representatives, and thus one obtains a well-defined element of 

:<math>\pi_{k+l-1}(X). </math>

==Grading==
Note that there is a shift of 1 in the grading (compared to the indexing of [[homotopy group]]s), so <math>\pi_k(X)</math> has degree <math>(k-1)</math>; equivalently, <math>L_k = \pi_{k+1}(X)</math> (setting ''L'' to be the graded quasi-Lie algebra). Thus <math>L_0 = \pi_1(X)</math> acts on each graded component.

==Properties==

The Whitehead product satisfies the following properties:

* Bilinearity.  <math>[f,g+h] = [f,g] + [f,h], [f+g,h] = [f,h] + [g,h]</math>
* Graded Symmetry. <math>[f,g]=(-1)^{pq}[g,f], f \in \pi_p X, g \in \pi_q X, p,q \geq 2</math>
* [[Graded Lie algebra|Graded Jacobi identity]]. <math>(-1)^{pr}[[f,g],h] + (-1)^{pq}[[g,h],f] + (-1)^{rq}[[h,f],g] = 0, f \in \pi_p X, g \in \pi_q X, h \in \pi_r X \text{ with } p,q,r \geq 2</math>

Sometimes the homotopy groups of a space, together with the Whitehead product operation are called a [[Graded Lie algebra|graded]] [[quasi-Lie algebra]]; this is proven in {{harvtxt|Uehara|Massey|1957}} via the [[Massey product|Massey triple product]].

=== Relation to the action of <math>\pi_{1}</math> ===

If <math>f \in \pi_1(X)</math>, then the Whitehead bracket is related to the usual action of <math>\pi_1</math> on <math>\pi_k</math> by

:<math>[f,g]=g^f-g, </math>

where <math>g^f</math> denotes the [[Inner automorphism|conjugation]] of <math>g</math> by <math>f</math>. 

For <math>k=1</math>, this reduces to

:<math>[f,g]=fgf^{-1}g^{-1}, </math>

which is the usual [[Commutator#Group theory|commutator]] in <math>\pi_1(X)</math>. This can also be seen by observing that the <math>2</math>-cell of the torus <math>S^{1} \times S^{1}</math> is attached along the commutator in the <math>1</math>-skeleton <math>S^{1} \vee S^{1}</math>.

=== Whitehead products on H-spaces ===

For a path connected [[H-space]], all the Whitehead products on <math>\pi_{*}(X)</math> vanish. By the previous subsection, this is a generalization of both the facts that the fundamental groups of H-spaces are abelian,
and that H-spaces are [[Simple space|simple]].

=== Suspension ===

All Whitehead products of classes <math>\alpha \in \pi_{i}(X)</math>, <math>\beta \in \pi_{j}(X)</math> lie in the kernel of the [[Suspension (topology)|suspension]] homomorphism <math>\Sigma \colon \pi_{i+j-1}(X) \to \pi_{i+j}(\Sigma X)</math>

==Examples==

* <math>[\mathrm{id}_{S^{2}} , \mathrm{id}_{S^{2}}] = 2 \cdot \eta \in \pi_3(S^{2})</math>, where <math>\eta \colon S^{3} \to S^{2}</math> is the [[Hopf fibration|Hopf map]].

This can be shown by observing that the [[Hopf invariant]] defines an isomorphism <math>\pi_{3}(S^{2}) \cong \Z</math> and explicitly calculating the cohomology ring of the cofibre of a map representing <math>[\mathrm{id}_{S^{2}}, \mathrm{id}_{S^{2}}]</math>. Using the [[Thom space|Pontryagin–Thom construction]] there is a direct geometric argument, using the fact that the preimage of a regular point is a copy of the [[Hopf link]].
